prompt.context: Edoceo is a leading global provider of integrated information solutions to business and professional customers. Customers depend on Edoceo for the information and information applications they need to make the right decisions to run their businesses. Edoceo provides information solutions for professionals across a broad range of industries and disciplines. Edoceo decided to outsource select HR processes including: Recruiting, Benefits Admin, HRIS, HR Admin, L&D, Compensation, Domestic Relocation, Expatriate Admin, Payroll, HR Contact Center. Edoceo is working with one of Deloitte's competitors to implement the outsourcing transition. The initiative's objective is to realize cost savings of 10%-20% of total current annual costs over five years, while maintaining equivalent levels of service. In parallel, Edoceo intends to transform the retained HR organization, creating internal Centers of Excellence (COE) and developing HR Business Partners to support with outsourced services. Edoceo has hired your team to provide best practice guidance and implementation leadership.
prompt.question: How would you design and implement optimal COEs and HR business partner capability for this organization and how would you structure the project? How would you describe a successful outcome for this project?

clarifying_info.q: What is driving the decision to outsource HR processes?
clarifying_info.a: Inefficiency and complexity of the existing HR organization were the driving forces of the outsourcing. There was also a broader cost reduction effort requiring a shift in HR support; Finance and IT were to follow.

clarifying_info.q: Which functions are intended for the Centers of Excellence?
clarifying_info.a: The functions intended for COEs are: Benefits, Compensation, Recruiting, Talent Management, HR Decision Support, L&D, Org Development, Diversity, and Policy, Compliance and M&A.

clarifying_info.q: What is the current state and vision for HR Business Partners?
clarifying_info.a: There is no current assessment of the HRBP role today, and each Market Group runs its own entity. The vision for the HRBP is to provide business unit specific and consultative services to executives and line managers for people-related issues impacting their business unit. Business Partners broker technical talent from the COEs to deliver HR solutions.

clarifying_info.q: What is the mood among retained HR staff?
clarifying_info.a: There is significant concern among staff in retained functions about the long-term safety of their jobs. Considerable job redesign and capability assessment will be conducted for retained positions.

framework: Plan & Assess: Conduct as-is inventory, define staffing strategy (COE and Business Partner), establish reporting and metrics strategy, perform stakeholder analysis, conduct change readiness assessment, develop communication and change strategy
Design: Process design for COE and Business Partner roles, build communication, change and training materials, and create implementation plan
Build & Implement: Build out process designs and COE structure, deliver training materials for new positions and processes
Support & Integrate: Ensure effective interactions with outsourced functions and the larger organization

questions.prompt: How would you structure the overall project to design and implement the COEs and HR Business Partner capability?
questions.guidance: Candidate should articulate a phased Plan-Build-Run (or equivalent) approach: (1) Plan & Assess — inventory current state, define COE and HRBP strategy, set metrics, conduct stakeholder and change readiness analysis, develop communication plan; (2) Design — design processes for COEs and HRBP roles, build training and change materials; (3) Build & Implement — stand up COE structures, deliver training; (4) Support & Integrate — monitor interactions with outsourced functions and broader org. Candidate should acknowledge that the focus is on organizational change management rather than purely financial analysis.

questions.prompt: What else should Edoceo be considering as it implements the outsourcing and development of the COEs?
questions.guidance: Candidate should raise additional risk and change management considerations beyond the structural design. Strong answers will cover: (1) Service disruption — risk of gaps in HR service delivery during transition; (2) Performance and morale issues — impact on productivity and engagement of retained and transitioning staff; (3) Attrition — potential loss of key talent who feel uncertain about their future roles; (4) Links to other initiatives — coordination with Finance and IT outsourcing efforts that are planned to follow. A structured framework (e.g., People/Process/Technology or risk categories) earns higher marks.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional considerations should Edoceo address as it implements the outsourcing and COE transformation?

categories.name: Service Continuity
ideas: Risk of service disruption during transition from in-house to outsourced processes
Need for parallel-run period to validate outsourced provider performance
Clear SLAs and governance model with the outsourcing vendor

categories.name: People and Change Management
ideas: Performance and morale issues among retained HR staff
Attrition risk — loss of institutional knowledge from departing employees
Transparent communication about job security and new role designs
Capability assessment and upskilling for staff moving into COE or HRBP roles

categories.name: Governance and Integration
ideas: Defining clear interfaces between HRBP, COE, and outsourced provider
Escalation paths and issue resolution processes
Metrics and KPIs to track both outsourced performance and COE effectiveness

categories.name: Links to Other Initiatives
ideas: Coordination with planned Finance and IT outsourcing efforts
Avoiding change fatigue from simultaneous large-scale transformations
Shared lessons learned and best practices across functions

recommendation: Design the retained HR organization around two pillars: COEs covering Benefits, Compensation, Recruiting, Talent Management, HR Decision Support, L&D, Org Development, Diversity, and Policy/Compliance/M&A; and HR Business Partners embedded in business units to broker COE expertise to line managers

Implement using a phased Plan-Build-Run approach with rigorous change management throughout, ensuring service continuity with the outsourcing vendor and clear governance between retained and outsourced functions
risks: Attrition of key HR talent during the uncertainty of transition
Service disruption if the outsourcing vendor is not properly integrated before in-house capabilities are wound down
Low adoption of new HRBP and COE model if change management and communication are insufficient
next_steps: Conduct as-is inventory and stakeholder analysis immediately
Stand up change readiness assessment and communication plan before any structural changes are announced
Define SLAs with outsourcing vendor and establish joint governance forum
Design HRBP and COE role profiles and begin capability gap assessment for retained staff
